content:
Let \(x\) satisfy

\[
x\equiv 1\pmod 5,\quad x\equiv 2\pmod 7,\quad x\equiv 3\pmod 9,\quad x\equiv 4\pmod{11}.
\]

Set \(x=1+5a\). Then

\[
1+5a\equiv 2\pmod 7 \implies 5a\equiv 1\pmod 7 \implies a\equiv 3\pmod 7.
\]

So \(a=3+7b\), giving

\[
x=16+35b.
\]

Now modulo \(9\),

\[
16+35b\equiv 3\pmod 9 \implies 7-b\equiv 3\pmod 9 \implies b\equiv 4\pmod 9.
\]

Thus \(b=4+9c\), so

\[
x=156+315c.
\]

Modulo \(11\),

\[
156+315c\equiv 4\pmod{11}
\implies 2+7c\equiv 4\pmod{11}
\implies 7c\equiv 2\pmod{11}.
\]

Since \(7^{-1}\equiv 8\pmod{11}\),

\[
c\equiv 16\equiv 5\pmod{11}.
\]

So \(c=5+11d\), and

\[
x=156+315(5+11d)=1731+3465d.
\]

The smallest positive solution is therefore

\[
\boxed{1731}.
\]
